In [[mathematics]], the '''Hodge bundle''', named after [[W. V. D. Hodge]], appears in the study of families of [[curve]]s, where it provides an [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] in the [[moduli theory]] of [[algebraic curve]]s. Furthermore, it has applications to the theory of [[modular form]]s on [[reductive group|reductive]] [[algebraic groups]]<ref>{{Citation

| isbn=978-3-540-74117-6
| doi=10.1007/978-3-540-74119-0

| location=Berlin

| series=Universitext
| mr=2409679 }}</ref> and [[string theory]].<ref>{{Citation

==Definition==
Let <math>\mathcal{M}_g</math> be the [[moduli space of algebraic curves]] of [[genus (mathematics)|genus]] ''g'' curves over some [[scheme (algebraic geometry)|scheme]]. The '''Hodge bundle''' <math>\Lambda_g</math> is a [[vector bundle]]<ref group=note>Here, "vector bundle" in the sense of [[quasi-coherent sheaf on an algebraic stack]]</ref> on <math>\mathcal{M}_g</math> whose [[vector bundle|fiber]] at a point ''C'' in <math>\mathcal{M}_g</math> is the space of [[holomorphic differential]]s on the curve ''C''. To define the Hodge bundle, let <math>\pi\colon \mathcal{C}_g\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_g</math> be the [[universal object|universal]] algebraic curve of genus ''g'' and let <math>\omega_g</math> be its [[relative dualizing sheaf]]. The Hodge bundle is the [[Direct image sheaf|pushforward]] of this sheaf, i.e.,<ref>{{Citation
| last1=Harris
| first1=Joe
| author1-link=Joe Harris (mathematician)
| last2=Morrison
| first2=Ian
| title=Moduli of curves
| year=1998
| series=[[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]]
| volume=187
| publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]]
| isbn=978-0-387-98429-2
| doi=10.1007/b98867
| mr=1631825
| page=155
}}</ref>
:<math>\Lambda_g=\pi_*\omega_g</math>.
